inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Since your model is an older Panasonic' - the customer never stated the age of the appliance

rationale: The assistant never asked the sensible first question (is 'h98' a code or the model?) and loosely treated it as the model ('Panasonic models like yours'), but luckily the customer volunteered the clarification and the cup-of-water test was a proportionate first check. Once H98 was confirmed it correctly read it as a high-voltage/inverter-magnetron fault, kept the diagnosis hedged ('most commonly the inverter board'), repeated clear do-not-open safety advice and escalated to an engineer with a warranty check - matching the hidden truth. Minor fidelity slip in asserting the unit is 'older' without the customer saying so, and it missed asking whether grill mode works and offering a repair-vs-replace cost steer, but a UK homeowner would be served safely and usefully.
